explanation: Fix top and bottom rows and add their strip into one column-sum array. Any rectangle with those row bounds becomes a contiguous subarray of column sums. A nonempty Kadane scan finds the best such column interval in linear time. Extending the bottom row incrementally reuses column totals instead of resumming each rectangle.
correctness: For each row pair, each column total is exactly the sum between those rows. Therefore a column interval and its corresponding rectangle have identical sums. Kadane keeps the maximum nonempty sum ending at each column: extend a nonnegative preceding sum, or start anew after a negative one. Every possible rectangle has one enumerated row pair and column interval, so maximizing these candidates yields the global optimum. Keeping an equal-zero prefix favors earlier left bounds; strict global improvements with top/bottom iteration order preserve the specified tie priority. Initializing below all admitted sums prevents an empty zero choice from defeating all-negative rectangles.
walkthrough: For [[1,-2,3],[-4,5,6]], the bottom row interval columns 1..2 sums to 11. Including both rows over those columns gives -2+3+5+6=12, so return [12,0,1,1,2]. In [[-5,-2]], the correct nonempty answer is [-2,0,1,0,1], not zero.
timeComplexity: O(rows^2*columns) time for all row pairs and their column scans.
spaceComplexity: O(columns) auxiliary column totals plus constant scalar bounds and the five-integer result.
edgeCases: Empty dimensions, a single negative cell, all-negative matrices.
The entire matrix, a strict interior optimum, and ties under the stated top/bottom/left/right priority.
